coverage.section: Appendix C: Graphical comparison of ψ functions

coverage.section: Appendix D: A more general boundary-crossing result

Proves equivalence of the one-sided Bernstein-type log-mgf condition and a quadratic sub-exponential condition by Taylor expansion and parameter adjustment; two-sided control requires the same for −X.
Bibliography for the local v8 manuscript.
Compares prior martingale tail bounds and motivates the paper’s conditional exponential-normalizer criterion.
States Theorem 2.1 and Corollaries 2.2–2.7: realized-square/V budgets, negative-third-moment, lower-increment, Bernstein, symmetry-truncation, and one-sided sub-Gaussian variants.
Applies the correctly matched inequalities to regression, autoregression and branching-process estimators via explicit martingale representations.
Uses stopped likelihood/change of measure, cubic negative-part control, conditional Bernstein expansion and symmetric truncation; this is the true source of the S007 general normalizer result.
Builds an exponential supermartingale from the intrinsic-time mgf condition and proves the piecewise variance-proxy estimate.
Verifies conditional moment and increment assumptions for the regression, autoregression and Galton–Watson examples.
Bibliography of the 22-page EJP paper.
Sets up one-sided supermartingale deviations and the conditional-square budget.
States the exact finite-n and simplified Hoeffding-type variance-budget inequalities.

Splits by the terminal bracket and optimizes the bracket cutoff using its exponential moment.
Bibliographic material.

Closing material and bibliography.

States Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.2 and the strengthened tail Theorem 2.3; records normal-range Cramér expansion, bracket-fluctuation extension, and limitations.

Builds exponential tilting, controls tilted drift and cumulant, compares a tilted martingale CLT to a Gaussian tail, and removes the bracket constraint by variance-filling/Rademacher extension.

Introduces exponential tilting, tilted drift and centered martingale, states Lemmas 3.1–3.4, and reduces the main theorem proof to the 2013 Bernstein-condition article; the detailed proof of Lemma 3.4 is not supplied.
Acknowledges reviewers and identifies the external Cramér, Bernstein-condition and tilted-CLT proof dependencies.
Bounds the tilted drift above and below by Taylor expansion, the conditional moment series, and the almost-sure bracket control.
Expands the log conditional moment generating function around its quadratic term and controls the remainder by Lemma 3.1 and the bracket error.
Defines the martingale bracket and Kolmogorov distance, reviews known rates, and states conditions A1–A2 and the exact-rate motivation.
States bracket-close and random-bracket Berry–Esseen bounds, sharpness examples, and the two bracket-crossing stopping indices.
Reduces rho by conditional Hölder, modifies predictable variance, and telescopes Gaussian-smoothed tests; conditional moment and bracket estimates control remainders.
Separates last-before and first-after bracket crossings and bounds the overshoot through the conditional variance assumption.
Stops near bracket one, adds independent Rademacher increments to fill the bracket, applies Theorem 2.1 and controls the added tail by Burkholder.
States technical lemmas used in the smoothing proof.
Bibliography.

Passes from finite to unbounded stopping under the paper’s integrability/limit conditions.
Applies the bounds to maxima and associated sequences, then to Wald-type identities with explicit centering assumptions.
Bibliography and publication metadata.

Constructs the predictable finite-variation compensator by localization and subsequence convergence; Theorem 2.3 gives uniqueness under the stated local integrability, with the difference a predictable finite-variation local martingale.

Contrasts the compensator-based construction with predictable/inaccessible decomposition and discusses its direct use in defining stochastic integrals; Appendix A starts on p.14.
Proves an expectation limsup lemma for uniformly integrable variables and monotone convergence lemmas for càdlàg maps/series, used in the existence arguments.
Bibliography.
Introduces martingale functional CLT motivation, continuous-limit setting and outline of the applications.

States Hypothesis 2.1 and the continuous-limit theorem, including diagonal limiting brackets, auxiliary martingale conditions and continuity/jump controls; proof identifies the Brownian limit under those hypotheses.
Uses Brownian local time and inverse local time to illustrate random-clock limits.
Derives the corresponding occupation-time limit for a random walk.
Applies the continuous-limit framework to the random comb process.
Proves tightness and convergence results for volatility models under the stated clock and bracket conditions.

Collects Lenglart’s inequality, Aldous’ criterion and bracket/martingale tightness criteria; Theorem A.3 relates C-tightness of martingales, quadratic variations and compensators under its moment hypotheses.
Algebraically derives alternative expressions for μ_v and c_v² from the finite-support occupation weights V, including its relation to B_V.
Bibliography begins after Appendix A.2 on physical p.16 and continues through p.18.
Introduces simplified semimartingale calculus, multiplicative compensators and change-of-measure aims.
Defines the stochastic-integrability class, real-coordinate calculus for complex processes, stochastic exponentials/logarithms and semimartingale representation.
Proves the interval-local martingale result and global extension under specialness; retains the jump exclusion ΔB^{L(Z)}≠−1.
Works out the independent-increment case and its multiplicative compensator.
Establishes the density/martingale transfer under its integrability and nonvanishing assumptions.
Summarizes scope and cites sources.

States the discrete atomless-innovation decomposition; Theorem 1.2 records the best-independent-L2 approximation lemma imported from [4], and the main proof sums the conditionally independent innovation series, checks the L2 energy identity, and uses characteristic functions for fixed-component increment independence.
Extends the discrete result to closed L2 martingales by reducing to a terminal variable and passing an L2 approximation; the conditional atomlessness hypothesis remains in force.

Develops the Brownian predictable-integrand decomposition. Lemma 3.1 and its iteration produce deterministic time factors; Proposition 3.2 characterizes scalar independent-increment Brownian martingales, and Theorem 3.4 applies Brownian martingale representation to decompose any scalar L2 Brownian martingale.
Explains the gain-process interpretation under a risk-neutral measure and notes the component martingales need not be mutually independent.

Uses Kunita–Watanabe representation and measurable matrix polar decomposition to obtain Theorem 5.4, a sum of Gaussian martingales with deterministic positive-semidefinite matrix factors and predictable orthogonal factors.
Bibliography; includes the earlier source [4] for the best-independent-L2 approximation lemma used but not proved in this note.
Introduces single-jump processes and the distinction among local martingales, semimartingales and endpoint integrability.
Defines locally absolutely continuous paths, the A_F^G integral and the finite-variation decomposition used for endpoint analysis.

States differential-subordination multiplier bounds and sharp scalar first-order Riesz transform estimates/stability questions.
Defines Hilbert-valued bracket, differential subordination and orthogonality; states sharp Burkholder and orthogonal inequalities and Bellman sufficient conditions.
Builds a finite martingale pair attaining the constants used in the stability estimates.
Constructs Bellman functions and proves near-extremizer stability below and above p=2.

Uses laminates and rank-one convexity to establish multiplier sharpness.
Represents scalar R_j by background-radiation Brownian integrals, applies the Bellman inequality and passes to the limit by Fatou.
Proves sharpness of the scalar transform conclusions and lists references.

Combines the embedding with a summability lemma to obtain continuous modifications and Holder estimates under p>d and beta<alpha-d/p.

Poses the Doob–Meyer compensator question for Snell envelopes and previews generator-domain and duality applications.

Assumption 3.2 is S1 and H1_loc; Theorem 3.3 proves dA=μ dD−, 0≤μ≤1 by partition approximation, conditional Snell comparison and Komlós averaging.
Under right-process, payoff integrability and g∈D(L), proves the value V lies in D(L) by identifying the compensator density.

Separates continuous and purely discontinuous ranges, independent-increment cases and one-sided estimates.
Treats Itô isomorphisms, Poisson random measures, UMD necessity, domination, approximations, canonical decomposition and covariation.

coverage.section: Front matter (title, author, abstract, contents start)

coverage.content_and_proof_mechanism: Develops unconditional and conditional Rényi quantities; proves the arbitrary-filtration conditional-Hölder upper bound, the i.i.d. flattened-family lower bound and nonattainment, and treats both divergence ceilings.

Summarizes the scope and open questions, then supplies bibliographic references.

coverage.section: Appendix A: Beyond the i.i.d. model
coverage.content_and_proof_mechanism: Extends conditional-Hölder bounds to general filtrations; conditional sharpness needs deterministic conditional divergences, and identifying the actual exponent requires an information-spectrum assumption.

coverage.section: Appendix B: Results quoted from the literature
coverage.content_and_proof_mechanism: States external results used in the paper (including Kolmogorov, Cramér, Chernoff–Stein, and Rényi facts) without proving them.

coverage.section: Front matter (title, author, provenance, date, contents)
coverage.content_and_proof_mechanism: Identifies the University of Bristol course notes, author, date and source provenance, and lists all eleven numbered sections; records document identity/scope rather than a theorem proof.

coverage.section: §1 A quick summary of some parts of measure theory
coverage.content_and_proof_mechanism: Defines algebras, σ-algebras, probability measures, measurable random variables and expectation; proves the continuity characterization of probability measures and gives construction examples, while Carathéodory extension is stated without proof.

coverage.section: §2 Conditional expectation and a toy example
coverage.content_and_proof_mechanism: States existence/uniqueness-a.s. of conditional expectation for integrable variables, computes conditional averages on a finite partition, illustrates independence from a σ-algebra, and states the tower rule without proof.

Proves Borel–Cantelli, monotone/Fatou/dominated convergence, Tonelli/Fubini, Jensen, Hölder and Minkowski results used later; proof routes include tail events, truncation by simple functions, nonnegative monotone limits, convex supporting lines and Hölder.
Defines weak, in-probability, a.s. and Lp convergence; proves an a.s.-Cauchy criterion and a.s.→probability→weak and Lp→probability implications, then gives counterexamples to converse implications.

Defines discrete filtrations, adapted martingales, predictable transforms/stochastic integrals and stopping times; proves stopped-process preservation by a predictable indicator, optional stopping by limit passage under bounded T, bounded X with T finite, or bounded increments plus ET<∞, and the nonnegative-supermartingale version by Fatou.

Proves Doob upcrossing via a predictable on/off transform, obtains a.s. finite convergence for L1-bounded supermartingales, and derives the L2 martingale criterion/convergence from orthogonal increments and a Pythagorean identity.

Constructs A_n=Σ_{k≤n}E[ΔX_k|F_{k−1}] and M_n=X_n−X_0−A_n, proves a.s. uniqueness and the submartingale iff A is nondecreasing criterion; for an L2 martingale from zero, identifies the predictable bracket compensator with increments E[(ΔM_n)^2|F_{n−1}].

Defines pth-power UI and proves absolute continuity of an L1 integral using Borel–Cantelli/Fatou; Theorem 8.3 states the Lp/UI/norm-moment equivalences under convergence in probability, while the notes supply only partial proofs (the p=1 UI directions, norm convergence, higher-moment-to-UI, domination-to-Lp) and explicitly skip the converse of Scheffé.

Proves UI martingale convergence and representation as conditional expectations, Lévy upward/downward convergence using UI and event-integral identities, Kolmogorov’s 0–1 law through conditional expectations, and the iid L1 strong law using a decreasing tail filtration.

For nonnegative discrete submartingales, partitions the maximal event by first crossing times F_k∈F_k and applies E[Z_n;F_k]≥E[Z_k;F_k]≥cP(F_k), yielding P(max_{k≤n}Z_k≥c)≤E[Z_n;max≥c]/c≤EZ_n/c; includes convex transforms and a cashier/random-walk application.

coverage.section: §11 A discrete Black–Scholes option pricing formula
coverage.content_and_proof_mechanism: In a finite independent binary-return model with −1<a<r<b, p=(r−a)/(b−a), and self-financing predictable holdings, proves discounted wealth is a martingale and every martingale has a unique predictable representation against the centered binary walk; conditional replication gives unique call price (1+r)^{−N}E_p[(S_N−K)^+] and monotonicity gives nonnegative stock holdings.
Lists Shiryaev and Williams as the cited foundational references; no additional theorem is established.
